title: Rare Pollinator Return Interval
dataSources: Bird acoustic detections (`birdnet:detection`), wildlife-camera visits (`wildlifecam:visit`), nest-box state (`nestbox:event`), frog-call activity (`frogcall:detection`), and pollinator counts (`pollinator:count`).
app: Wildlife telemetry from BirdNET, trail and feeder cameras, nest-box sensors, frog-call detectors, and pollinator counters streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted imports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pollinator:count rare=1
| sort 0 _time
| streamstats current=f last(_time) as prev_time by species
| eval days_between=round((_time-prev_time)/86400,1)
| stats avg(days_between) as avg_days_between max(days_between) as max_days_between by species
| sort - max_days_between
description: Measures how often rarely seen pollinators return between observations.
value: Return intervals help you distinguish a truly rare visitor from one you simply have not measured consistently before.
implementation: Tag uncommon pollinator visits from camera or manual counts and keep species naming stable over time.
visualization: Table of average and maximum days between sightings by species.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how long it usually takes before a rare pollinator comes back again.
